channel.title: Social Media Today - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Social Media Today (socialmediatoday.com)

item.title: Instagram introduces thumbnail post editing for grids
item.description: The new feature allows users to choose how images and clips will be displayed, adding another element of profile customization.

item.title: Pinterest releases best practices tip sheet for shopping templates
item.description: The tips are designed to help social media marketers and brands make product pins stand out on the app.

item.title: TikTok publishes latest EU usage, enforcement data
item.description: The update provided insight into how the app dealt with information requests and moderation rules in the second half of 2025.

item.title: X tests experimental topic feed filter
item.description: The For You tab feature is designed to allow users to access a more focused version of their timelines, centered around chosen subject matter.

item.title: Instagram opens up content scheduling to all users
item.description: The feature was previously only available to Professional Mode users, but this update will allow anyone on the app to access the expanded creator tool.

item.title: X launches paid partnership labels for sponsored content
item.description: The new option is designed to provide additional transparency for brand partnerships and align the app with other social media platforms.

item.title: U.S. Supreme Court declines to hear AI copyright case
item.description: The decision upheld a lower court ruling that artificial intelligence-generated content does not have the same legal protections as human-created work.

item.title: Concerns with third party partner could derail LinkedIn’s verification push
item.description: The company has continued to add more identification checks and balances, but questions remain regarding its verification partner Persona.

item.title: Almost half of the U.S. consumers use TikTok as a search engine
item.description: The app’s use as a discovery tool is rising as users turn to its short-form videos and personalized content to find information, according to research from Adobe.

item.title: More teen social media bans are coming, but will they work?
item.description: While the world attempts to limit underage access to apps, teenagers continue to find new ways to bypass rules and undermine systems.
